title: What a ShieldCare Plan May Be Sold On, and When It Comes into Force
content:
## Clause 1: the item

A Northbeam ShieldCare Protection Plan is sold only on an item whose recorded purchase price
falls inside the plan's price band and whose department is one the plan covers. The price and
the department are read from the item as recorded against the sale, correlated to the plan by
the serial of the item to be covered, and settled before the plan is written rather than
afterwards.

## Clause 2: the age of the item

A plan is added to an item already owned only when the day the item was bought is no further
back than the plan's item age limit. The item age limit is counted in calendar days from the
item purchase day, which counts as day zero, and a plan sold on the same receipt as the item
always meets it. The recorded purchase day of the item is the authority for the count; the
comparison is that the day of purchase must be no earlier than the limit allows, and a day
falling exactly on the limit satisfies it.

### Both sides of the age limit

Take a plan whose item age limit is 60 days and an item bought on day zero. A plan written on the sixtieth day
after that purchase day meets the limit, because the boundary day itself is inside it. A plan written on the
sixty-first day does not. Calendar days are counted
throughout, so a weekend or a day the stores are shut is counted like any other.

## Clause 3: business profiles and business use

ShieldCare Business Fleet Protection is sold only on a profile recorded as a business. Use of
an item in a business where the item is covered by a consumer plan is outside cover, rather
than a reason to void the plan.

## Clause 4: activation and the coverage window

A plan is activated when the single premium has cleared, or when the first instalment has
cleared on an instalment plan. The coverage window then runs from what the plan's coverage
start basis names, for the term of months sold.

## Clause 5: a plan that was never eligible

Where the item turns out never to have been eligible, or the serial given at the sale belongs
to no purchase on file, the plan is declared void, every premium taken is returned less
nothing, and no claim is paid from it. A plan that is void was never in force: it is not a
cancellation, and the customer keeps no free-look right to argue about.

## Points of judgement

| Fact recorded | Admission |
| --- | --- |
| Price inside the band, department covered, plan sold on the same receipt | Admitted |
| Price inside the band, item bought further back than the age limit allows | Not admitted |
| Price below the band's inclusive minimum | Not admitted |
| Consumer plan, item later used in a business | Plan stands; the business use is outside cover |
| Serial belongs to no purchase on file | Void, with every premium returned less nothing |
